scope.description: Whole calc application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: Workbook creation/editing, formulas, formatting/charts, data import/analysis, pivot tables and spreadsheet interaction.

coverage.rationale: Typed labelled rows and captured CSV now preserve identifiers, literal notes and declared missing measurements alongside the existing numeric summaries and requirements. This deepens the table-publication family; broad spreadsheet editing, formatting, charts, pivoting, formulas and automation remain absent, so the coarse whole-application estimate remains 10%.

scope.description: Declared numeric or typed text/number tables, captured CSV with explicit column/null policy, verified editable workbook publication, numeric summaries and requirements, including a declared producer-file handoff.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Table schemas, literal labels, missingness, summaries and requirements hide native conversion and recalculation. Authors still declare types, null policy and supported measurements; native workbook limits remain explicit. These additions retain the existing 80% estimate within this named workflow family.

limitations: Bounded tables and fixed numeric summaries, not general workbook editing. Each numeric column needs at least two present values; empty text is refused, null becomes blank, and text never enters numeric summaries.

Native workbook numbers allow documented decimal rounding and negative-zero normalisation. Use text for exact identifiers and integers above 2^53. No authored formulas, macros, dates, currency or unit inference.
A generic file artifact is parsed against an explicit CSV header, types and null policy before native work; file kind alone does not establish compatible table contents.
Subjective source-contract assessment, not an exhaustive API measurement. Native availability, actual runtime observations and source-bound qualification are separate facts.
